patterns.name: Segmented N-tier application
guidance: Preserve web, application, and data tiers as separate scaling and network boundaries.
For VM-based tiers, associate each tier with its own subnet and restrict data-tier ingress to the application tier.
Represent each visible load balancer, VM, VM scale set, NSG, and subnet separately.

sources.name: Azure Architecture Center: N-tier architecture style

patterns.name: Secure App Service and SQL three-tier application
guidance: Keep the web App Service, API App Service, and Azure SQL Database as distinct deployable resources.
Only create private endpoints, private DNS zones, or VNet integration when they are visible in the diagram.
Prefer managed identity and Microsoft Entra authentication over embedded SQL credentials.
A public Application Gateway or WAF is ingress, not a replacement for either App Service tier.

Azure Architecture Center: App Service baseline

patterns.name: Serverless static web application with Functions and Cosmos DB
guidance: Preserve Static Web Apps, Function Apps, Cosmos DB, Storage, Key Vault, and monitoring as distinct services.
Private endpoints and VNet integration must follow the drawn app and data subnet boundaries.
Use managed identity for service access and do not turn pipeline or source artifacts into Azure resources.

patterns.name: AKS platform with multiple application workloads
guidance: A single AKS boundary containing multiple workload icons is one cluster with multiple Kubernetes workloads.
Generate Kubernetes Deployments and Services for visible workloads; container images are build artifacts, not clusters.
Keep cluster infrastructure, ingress, registry, identity, networking, and in-cluster manifests separate.

patterns.name: IBM Maximo Application Suite on Azure Red Hat OpenShift
guidance: Preserve Azure Red Hat OpenShift as ARO; never translate it into AKS.

Model the ARO control-plane and worker subnets, public and internal load balancers, NSGs, DNS zones, ExpressRoute gateway, Bastion, Azure Files shares, optional jump box, and SQL Managed Instance only when visible.
ARO managed control-plane and worker-node labels describe cluster configuration, not independent Azure VM resources.

Generate one Microsoft.RedHatOpenShift/openShiftClusters@2025-07-25 resource for the visible ARO service. Treat the managed control-plane and worker-node labels as profiles of that cluster, not separate resources.

Use the supported service-principal ARO form for concise generated IaC. Keep aroVersion and aroClientId as required string parameters, and aroClientSecret and aroPullSecret as required @secure string parameters. Never use defaults or placeholders for these values.

Map aroClientId and aroClientSecret to servicePrincipalProfile, aroPullSecret to clusterProfile.pullSecret, the visible control-plane subnet to masterProfile.subnetId, and the visible worker subnet to workerProfiles[0].subnetId.
Put aroVersion inside clusterProfile.version. clusterProfile.resourceGroupId must identify a distinct ARO-managed resource group, not resourceGroup().id.

Set masterProfile.vmSize. Set each worker profile name, count, diskSizeGB, vmSize, and subnetId. When the visible subnets have NSGs, set networkProfile.preconfiguredNSG to Enabled and state that the ARO service principal needs the documented network permissions.

Add manualActions to register Microsoft.RedHatOpenShift, Microsoft.Compute, Microsoft.Storage, and Microsoft.Authorization; verify at least 44 regional vCPUs and selected VM SKU availability; validate IBM MAS, OpenShift, and ARO version compatibility; grant the ARO service principal required network permissions; and provide every required parameter.
Add a manualAction to install IBM Maximo Application Suite with IBM-supported Marketplace or automation after ARO is ready. Keep this action as a Bicep comment so MAS is not silently omitted.
Emit actual Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/fileServices/shares child resources for the visible Premium NFS and Standard SMB Azure Files shares. Do not move share creation into manualActions.
Azure SQL Managed Instance is supported in this pattern; do not substitute Azure SQL Database or Cosmos DB.
If SQL Managed Instance is emitted, use an @secure administrator-password parameter with a newGuid() default; never hard-code a password.
Do not invent Kubernetes manifests for IBM Maximo. MAS installation requires IBM-supported automation and version compatibility inputs that are not encoded in the architecture diagram.
Twilio SendGrid is a third-party service. If it is detected, list it as unsupported, add a manualAction to configure it separately, and do not replace it with Azure Communication Services.
